recommended_next_phase: An ordinary implementation phase building exactly scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py and scripts/hatp_principal_signer_admin.py per this phase's selected architecture (Section 15/18 of the phase report). No hardware touched. HMIC scope expansion not bundled unless a future re-derivation finds sound reason to combine it. Not authorized here.
summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2L is an analysis/sequencing-only phase (no Trust-Enrollment real effect performed). It independently re-verified the entering real state claimed by its own prompt against primary repo evidence rather than trusting it blindly, confirming HMIC v1.6 active/VALID (certification_id=2e5f861249d8e70bff53ba2f371d84e37e14eff0bbfcd939902fa7b47d236bd7), 36 frozen files / 7 bound contracts (HMIC-001 v1.6, HBDC-001 v1.2, HPSE-001 v1.1, HHCE-001 v1.1, HSCE-001 v1.3, HMRC-001 v1.1, HATP-001 v1.0), and HardwareCredentialRecord/Principal/Signer/DeploymentBinding all still absent, Class-B still NON_COMPLIANT on HBDC-REQ-042. It found and corrected a stale claim in its own phase prompt (Section 19's 'six readiness terms' claim): the production readiness conjunction in hatp_mandatory_cutover.py currently constructs eight terms, not six, and only two remain unmet (hatp_substrate_operational, class_b_deployment_conformance_satisfies_readiness), both strictly downstream of the same missing Trust-Enrollment chain -- proved by reading human_approval_trusted_provenance.py's inspect_hatp_verification_substrate_readiness() and hatp_bootstrap.py's HATPTrustStore, which resolve load_repository_enrollment/lookup_authority through the identical registry.json DeploymentBinding/Principal/Signer records the Trust-Enrollment writers produce (no separate parallel state, no DAG cycle). It traced the full production FIDO2 (hatp_fido2_provider.py Fido2HardwareProvider.enroll_credential, Surface A) -> HardwareCredentialRecord (hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py register_credential, Surface B, contractually separate transition from Surface A per HHCE-001) -> Principal/Signer (hatp_principal_signer_admin.py enroll_principal/enroll_signer, Surface C, HPSE-REQ-057's continuous two-lock ordering across .hardware-credential-transition.lock outer + .deployment-binding-transition.lock inner) -> DeploymentBinding (hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py create_deployment_binding, which directly cross-validates an active PrincipalRecord, an active matching SignerRecord, and an active matching HardwareCredentialRecord before any write) chain directly from current production source, confirming all four library writers already exist and are already HMIC-bound at v1.5 (Phase 149O.20L.7O.2H). It freshly re-confirmed (not assumed from 2K.4/2K.5) that the standalone scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py and scripts/hatp_principal_signer_admin.py admin entrypoints still do not exist on the filesystem, and that cli.py has zero Trust-Enrollment dispatch -- library implementation exists (A), public governed admin entrypoint does not (B), so the correct next scope is exactly two standalone scripts mirroring the existing scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py / scripts/hatp_deployment_binding_admin.py precedent, never a CLI extension (routing high-privilege administration through the agent-reachable CLI was explicitly considered and rejected on HHCE-REQ-019/020/HPSE-REQ-028/029 security-architecture grounds). It designed the failure-after-hardware-creation recovery path (Surface A/B's deliberate transaction separation means a makeCredential success followed by a register_credential failure leaves the physical credential intact and retryable via the identical CredentialEnrollmentEvidence, made safe by _candidate_equal idempotency, no orphaned/unrecoverable state). Its single load-bearing finding: reading hatp_mandatory_certification.py's own _FROZEN_REPOSITORY_ROOT_RELATIVE_FILES constant directly proved the two new scripts, once written, would NOT be members of the current 36-file HMIC-bound set (only the two existing precedent scripts are bound there) -- applying HMIC-REQ-052's own test (could modifying the new script while all 36 currently-bound bytes stay unchanged alter an authority-bearing Trust-Enrollment result -- yes, because the script is the sole caller turning human intent into calls against the already-bound writers), both new scripts must become HMIC-bound (a future v1.7 source-scope evolution) before real Trust-Enrollment use, and the current active certification would become source-parity-stale the moment the scripts exist as production-authoritative code, requiring a fresh CertificationRecord/activation before real use -- a major sequencing consequence this phase derived rather than assumed. Selected verdict: A + C (architecture frozen, implementation ready, future HMIC binding required before real use). Twelve focused architecture/evidence tests were added (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7o_2l_post_hmic_activation_trust_enrollment_dag.py) covering admin-script/library existence and absence, HMIC frozen-scope membership (library bound, scripts not bound), the 36-file/7-contract counts, DeploymentBinding cross-validation source assertions, the corrected 8-term readiness-conjunction text assertions, the substrate/registry unification proof, DAG cycle-freedom (13 nodes, 16 edges, formal DFS), and next-implementation-prerequisite predecessor-satisfaction assertions -- all 12 pass. Full regression: python -m pytest -n auto -m fast_green -q ran the complete suite: 8240 passed, 7 skipped, 126.37s runtime. Non-passing node counts are identical to 2K.5's own confirmed baseline; the passed count increased by exactly 12, matching this phase's own 12 new tests one-for-one. This phase's own attributable regression count: 0 failed. No src/pcae production file, contract file, or Protected-Root-adjacent artifact was touched -- only this phase's own doc, its companion test file, CHANGELOG.md, PROJECT_STATUS.md, .pcae metadata/report, and task-lifecycle files were changed, confirmed by git status/diff --stat. No HardwareCredentialRecord/Principal/Signer/DeploymentBinding was created; no FIDO2 hardware was touched; no HMIC certification was altered; no readiness term changed value; no HATP activation occurred. pcae health healthy, pcae check passed, pcae status coherence coherent, pcae doctor task-memory warnings (pre-existing, unrelated), pcae push check clean pre-finalization, pcae runtime inspect unchanged (Observed/observe/unavailable/not_implemented).
